name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,723

clue.text: Pipe is turned back; new plumbing at last stopping flood

indicators.note: something turned back faces the other way, so the letters are read from right to left
at last points to the final position, so only the closing letter of the word is kept
to stop a gap is to plug it, so these letters sit inside the other piece

blocks.note: a flue is a pipe or duct carrying smoke from a fire
N is the standard abbreviation for new
the final letter of plumbing

explanation.surface: A plumber's notes on a flood: a pipe has twisted round, and the new plumbing is finally holding back the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed pipe EULF opens after its first letter to take N and G, giving E-NG-ULF.
explanation.definitionFit: To engulf is to swamp or overwhelm with water, which is exactly what a flood does to land or buildings.

clue.text: One's left out of European threesome: keeping English for all time

indicators.note: something left out of a group is omitted, so that letter is dropped from the word
to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds the other inside

blocks.note: one is the Roman numeral I
E is the abbreviation for European
a trinity is a group of three
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone drops out of a three-person European team, which hangs on to its English member forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is I as a Roman numeral, so 'one's left out' removes an I; the second E then slots in after the opening two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is endless time without beginning or end, the whole of time considered together, a direct synonym phrase.

clue.text: Encouraging reports of old comedians going round St Paul's?

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: the Goons were the comedy team of the 1950s radio programme The Goon Show
St Paul's Cathedral in London is famous for its great dome

explanation.surface: Tourists hear cheering accounts of veteran comics touring St Paul's Cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goons (Spike Milligan, Peter Sellers, Harry Secombe) split as GOO...NS around DOME. The question mark flags St Paul's as an example: the cathedral stands for its dome.
explanation.definitionFit: Good omens are favourable signs or portents, things that bring hopeful news about what is going to happen.

clue.text: Ignores out-of-bounds yob

indicators.note: the bounds of a word are its two ends, and putting them out leaves only the inside letters

blocks.note: to flout a rule is to ignore it openly

explanation.surface: A thug pays no attention to signs marking forbidden ground.
explanation.walkthrough: FLOUTS loses its first and last letters to leave LOUT. 'Out-of-bounds' reads as a single adjective describing the yob, but it is the instruction to strip the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A yob is a British word for a rough, uncouth young man, and a lout is the same sort of boorish person.

clue.text: Crazy man kidnaps Heath, Statesman

indicators.note: something crazy is disordered, so the letters come out in a jumbled arrangement
a kidnapper holds a captive, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Erica is the botanical name for heath or heather

explanation.surface: A deranged man abducts Edward Heath, the former British Prime Minister and statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath looks like Edward Heath, British Prime Minister 1970-74, but it is the plant. The definition splits Statesman as States-man: a man from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as States-man, a statesman is a man from the States, which is a citizen of the USA, an American.

clue.text: Shy rodent suffering internal reflex: it's often seen standing on hind legs

definitions.text: it's often seen standing on hind legs

indicators.note: a reflex bends back on itself, and an internal one turns round only the letters in the middle of the word

blocks.note: meek means timid or retiring
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A timid rodent with some inner nervous reaction, typically rearing up on its back legs.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'internal reflex' turns round only the two letters where the words meet, leaving both ends in place; the definition is a description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Meerkats famously stand upright on their back feet as sentries, watching for predators across the African scrub.

clue.text: Unexpectedly go to war in British vessel

indicators.note: something that happens unexpectedly breaks the expected order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A nation suddenly enters a war aboard a British warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In British vessel' reads as a place, but 'in' is fodder alongside the letters of 'go to war' and B.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing boat is a small craft propelled by oars, and any boat is a vessel in the general sense.

clue.text: Pick 100-500 sheets of paper

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
a ream is 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: An instruction at the stationer's: choose a quantity of between one and five hundred sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: '100-500' looks like a range of numbers but is two separate pieces: 100 on its own, and 500 sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: The pick of a group is its best part, and the cream is likewise the finest selection, as in the cream of the crop.

clue.text: Legwear only tossed between partners

indicators.note: something tossed is thrown about, so its letters land in a new arrangement
something placed between two things is flanked by them, so it goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Stockings are flung back and forth between a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the four players are named by compass point, and North-South form one partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings made from nylon fibre, so they are a kind of legwear in everyday use.

clue.text: Launch list of international delegates?

blocks.note: the UN, the United Nations, is the international body of national delegates
a roll is an official list of names

explanation.surface: An announcement that a list of foreign representatives is being published.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the cryptic reading: a roll of delegates to the United Nations would be a UN roll.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch a campaign or product is to roll it out or unroll it, setting it going for the public to see.

clue.text: Expressive performance of Queen with cello, leaving out middle part unfortunately

indicators.note: leaving out the middle part means the central letter of the word is dropped
things that turn out unfortunately go awry, so the letters end up out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
cello with its central letter dropped

explanation.surface: A review of a rock band's concert: Queen played with a cellist, but the middle section was sadly cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen wants to be the rock band or ER, but it is taken whole as fodder. CELLO has five letters, so its middle one is the third, an L.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloquence is fluent, persuasive and moving speech, which is a forceful, expressive use of language in performance.

clue.text: Turn round with order for Rover?

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
Heel! is the command telling a dog to walk close behind

explanation.surface: A dog trainer tells the dog to turn round.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover is a stock name for a dog; the question mark flags that Rover is just an example of one.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to pivot or swing about, as soldiers wheel on parade, so it means turn round.

clue.text: Approval withheld for shelter

blocks.note: withholding consent is saying no
an OK is approval

explanation.surface: Planning permission is refused for a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read literally: approval is OK, and approval withheld is NO OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small, sheltered corner or recess, a secluded spot offering protection and retreat.

clue.text: They may enjoy club where ladies entertain: one piece after another

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them into your home, so the hosting letters wrap round the guests
one thing coming after another sets them side by side in a fixed order

blocks.note: ladies are women
R is the chess notation for a rook, another piece
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: Men frequent a club where the ladies put on a show, one act after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' means a chess piece, and 'another' is a second one, the rook, written R in chess notation. A working men's club is a British social club for manual workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Working men's clubs were founded for labourers, so working men are the members who would enjoy one.

clue.text: Doris, maybe 27, accompanied by journalist, wasn't paying attention

blocks.note: Doris Day was the American singer and film star
the answer to clue 27, imagine
ED, short for editor, is a stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Doris, perhaps the 27-year-old, out with a reporter, wasn't listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doris, maybe' signals a surname: Doris is one example of a Day. The 27 refers to the answer at 27-across.
explanation.definitionFit: To daydream is to let the mind drift into pleasant fantasy, so someone daydreaming is distracted and inattentive.

clue.text: Sean was regularly interrupting work for digital growth

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so every other letter is taken
to interrupt is to break into the middle, so these letters go inside the other piece

blocks.note: toil is hard work
the even letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Sean kept butting in on a project about the growth of the digital economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests computers, but digits are also fingers and toes.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a toe as well as a finger, and a toenail is the horny plate that grows on one.

clue.text: Island also claiming catch

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: too means also
to bag is to catch, as a hunter bags game

explanation.surface: An island nation also lays claim to a fishing haul.
explanation.walkthrough: Tobago is the smaller island of Trinidad and Tobago in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a Caribbean island lying north-east of Trinidad, so it is a straightforward example of an island.

clue.text: Drag a very dilapidated area for bodies

indicators.note: something dilapidated has fallen apart, so the letters are in a broken-down new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Police trawl a run-down patch of ground looking for corpses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag' suggests searching a river for a body, which fits the surface, but it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A graveyard is a burial ground, a plot of land set aside where the dead are laid to rest.

clue.text: Love to be immersed in stormy sea-mist sprays

indicators.note: something immersed is plunged inside, so one piece sits within the other
stormy weather churns everything up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A romantic picture: love lost in the spray of a stormy sea mist.
explanation.walkthrough: The blocks run in answer order: the O lands inside the rearranged sea-mist letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To atomise a liquid is to break it into a fine mist of droplets, which is what spraying it does.

clue.text: Did undergo some enhancement, dropping team of beginners

indicators.note: beginners are the ones who start, so the first letter of each word is taken

blocks.clueFragment: undergo some enhancement, dropping team of
blocks.note: the opening letters of these six words

explanation.surface: Someone had some improvement work done but quit the training squad for novices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Team of beginners' looks like a squad of novices, but 'team of' is fodder and 'beginners' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Used to expresses past habit, as in I used to swim, and the auxiliary did can stand in the same way.

clue.text: America supports rising drug firm? It employs suckers!

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so the letters run backwards
in a down clue, a support sits underneath, so this piece comes last

blocks.note: pot is slang for cannabis
CO is the abbreviation for company
US is the United States

explanation.surface: The US backs a growing pharmaceutical company, a business that cons gullible customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suckers' are dupes in the surface, but the definition means the suction cups on tentacles.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus grips prey and surfaces with the rows of suction cups along its eight arms, so it literally uses suckers.

clue.text: Result of dehydration in the main?

definitions.text: Result of dehydration in the main?

blocks.note: surface reading: what happens to a body that has lost too much water
setter's reading: the main is the ocean, so this is what is left when ocean water evaporates

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' passes for 'mostly', but the main is an old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Evaporating ocean water in pans leaves crystals behind, so this product is the residue of drying out the brine.

clue.text: Amputee on board lives poorly on rum initially

indicators.note: something done poorly is done badly, so the letters come out wrongly arranged
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of rum

explanation.surface: A one-legged sailor lives badly, surviving mainly on rum.
explanation.walkthrough: Long John Silver is the one-legged pirate of Treasure Island; 'on board' puts him on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver, the ship's cook in Stevenson's novel, has lost a leg, so he is the amputee at sea.

clue.text: Suit creased: a psychopath wrapping it up

indicators.note: something wrapping an object encloses it, so the letters sit inside the words
in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word, the a, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A creased suit: a psychopath is bundling up the evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' at the start looks like clothing, given 'creased', but it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards, alongside hearts, diamonds and clubs.

clue.text: For example, bolt screen to uncovered tiles

indicators.note: uncovering something strips off its outer layer, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: to screen a film is to project it
tiles without its outer letters

explanation.surface: DIY instructions: for example, fix a screen to bare tiles with a bolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' looks like a fixing screw in the DIY surface, but it is the short arrow fired from a crossbow.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow bolt is a missile shot through the air, so it is one example of a thing that is fired.

clue.text: Shown in Europe, Ravel's works

indicators.note: something shown in a display sits inside it, so the letters are inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: The compositions of Ravel are being performed across Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Opera here is the plural of opus, which suits Ravel and is not the staged drama it first suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is the Latin plural of opus, a numbered musical composition, so it means a composer's works.

clue.text: A woman stripped twice for hairdo

indicators.note: stripping takes off the outer layer, and doing it twice removes two letters from each end

blocks.note: a supermum is a mother who copes brilliantly with everything

explanation.surface: A woman undresses twice before getting her hair done.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPERMUM loses S and M, then U and U, to leave PERM.
explanation.definitionFit: A perm, short for permanent wave, is a hairstyle in which curls are set chemically to last for months.

clue.text: Makers of supplies missing nothing out

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: goods are supplies or merchandise
nothing is zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Manufacturers of provisions are running short of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makers of supplies' reads as manufacturers, but 'Makers' stands alone and 'of' joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In many religions gods are creators of the world, so they are makers in the sense of the Maker.

clue.text: Imagine mother taking religious lessons!

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a dam is an animal's mother
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: Fancy that: mum is going to religious classes!
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for Religious Education, a subject taught in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream of something is to picture it in the mind, so as a verb it is a synonym for imagine.

clue.text: Once coating of oil left out, are rollmops bad for teeth?

indicators.note: a coating is the outside layer, so only the outer letters of the word are taken
letters that are left out are removed from the rest
something gone bad is spoilt, so these letters are rearranged into another order

blocks.note: the first and last letters of oil
taken as written

explanation.surface: Once the oil is drained off, are pickled herrings harmful to your teeth?
explanation.walkthrough: Rollmops are rolled pickled herring fillets. Remove O and L from 'are rollmops' and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Premolars are the grinding teeth between the canines and molars, so they are one particular kind of tooth.

clue.text: David Essex song introduction involving drums, oddly

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, so the first, third and fifth letters are kept
to involve is to wrap up or include, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the start is the introduction or opening
the odd letters of drums

explanation.surface: A David Essex song opens with a quirky drum intro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduction' looks like part of the song, but it is a synonym; David Essex was a 1970s British pop star.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardust was a 1974 hit single for David Essex, from the film of the same name in which he starred.

clue.text: Principal musical numbers; they're delivered sotto voce?

blocks.note: first meaning: the main tracks on vinyl singles, as opposed to the flip sides
second meaning: remarks spoken in an undertone, as by an actor to the audience

explanation.walkthrough: Split as A-sides, the first reading is record tracks; sotto voce is Italian for under the breath, the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: On a single the lead track is the A-side, and in theatre an aside is a quiet remark meant only for the audience.
